subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the value of k if the points (1,3), (2,k) are conjugate with respect to the circle x² + y² = 35.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, SENIOR INTER MATHS-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.79 — VSAQ chapter 12 Circle, answer 113.1. insider_note: For a circle centred at the origin the condition collapses to x₁x₂ + y₁y₂ = r², which is one line — no g, no f, no c to carry.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the conjugate points condition
steps.margin_note: One mark. The circle is centred at the origin, so g = f = 0 and the condition is short.
steps.memory_tip: Two points are conjugate when S₁₂ = 0.
lines: Two points are conjugate with respect to
steps.why: Two points are conjugate when each lies on the polar of the other, and writing that out gives S₁₂ = 0. With the centre at the origin there are no linear terms, so only the product terms and the constant survive.
common_mistakes: Using S₁₁ instead of S₁₂ and putting one point in twice.

steps.label: Substitute and solve for k
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply the x-coordinates together and the y-coordinates together, then subtract 35.
steps.why: Substituting both points gives a single linear equation in k. Only the y-coordinates carry the unknown, so it is solved in one step.
common_mistakes: Pairing x₁ with y₂ instead of x₂.
